title: Juniper and the Asset
premise: Mara Marchetti, a peace-delegation interpreter who has survived three years of shifting rules by staying invisible, receives a calendar invitation from her handler — sent after his death. The meeting pulls her into a botched extraction of Anton Voss, a defector whose memory holds the delegation's buried secrets, and Mara realizes she was chosen not for her skills but because she is expendable. As hunters close in and Voss's account of the past contradicts everything Mara remembers of her own recruitment, she must decide whether survival means delivering him or burning the network that made them both bait. In the end, Mara trades the defector's testimony to a rival faction for passage out, keeping only one recording — proof that her own missing memories were taken, not lost.
about_author: Coral Thornbury is the pen name of a former NGO field coordinator who spent a decade in contested border regions before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose languages, loyalties, and memories are never entirely their own.

chapters.title: The Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. During a fractious delegation dinner in Geneva, Mara receives a calendar invite from Handler Elias Brandt — timestamped hours after his confirmed death. The location is a hotel two streets away. Torn between protocol and instinct, she goes, finding only a burner phone with one instruction: 'Voss lands at 06:00. You are the interpreter.' The beat is dread disguised as routine; Mara realizes the rules have finally rewritten her.

chapters.title: Six O'Clock Cargo
chapters.summary: Alternating Mara and Voss POVs. The extraction half-succeeds: Mara smuggles Voss out of the airport past teams that should not know he exists, but the safe house is already burned. Voss claims Brandt was killed because he tried to cancel the operation — and that Mara's recruitment file contains pages she has never seen. The emotional beat is vertigo: her competence becomes her cage as she realizes she was selected precisely because no one will miss her.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with Voss's recorded testimony threaded through. Cornered in a riverside boathouse, Mara decodes Brandt's final message: Voss's memory is the asset, and the delegation's peace talks were cover for laundering it. A trusted colleague from the delegation arrives — as the hunters' inside man. Mara must choose between handing over Voss to save herself or trusting a stranger's broken recollections of her own past. Climax: she turns the exchange into an ambush, and the river takes the evidence — except the copy she hides on her body.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Silence
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Wounded and officially erased, Mara negotiates her exit with a rival faction, offering Voss's testimony while withholding the recording that proves her memories were surgically altered during recruitment. Voss walks free into a new identity; Mara walks into an older one. The resolution is quiet and costly: belonging, she understands, was always a translation error — but the price of survival is a truth she now carries alone, untranslated.
